title: Habitats: A Framework for Open-Ended Evolution of Agent Objectives
abstract: arXiv:2611.31160v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Designing what an agent should optimize can be as difficult as optimizing the agent itself. Existing language-model-based reward-generation methods typically refine objectives for predefined tasks and couple the decision of what to explore with the synthesis of how to implement it, potentially narrowing the resulting behavioral repertoire. We introduce Habitats, a framework for open-ended evolution of executable agent objectives. Habitats maintains a population of reward-policy pairs and evaluates every policy under every population reward, producing a cross-fitness matrix that exposes self-mastery, transfer, and functional diversity. A population-level Planner uses this information to select parent rewards and issue targeted mutation directives, while a separate Mutator translates those directives into validated reward programs. translated_title: Habitats：一个面向智能体目标的开放式演化框架
translated_abstract: 设计智能体应当优化什么，其难度不亚于优化智能体本身。现有的基于语言模型的奖励生成方法通常只是针对预定义任务来细化目标，并将“探索什么”的决策与“如何实现”的合成耦合在一起，这可能使最终获得的行为库变得狭窄。我们提出了Habitats，一个用于智能体可执行目标开放式演化的框架。Habitats维护一个由奖励-策略对组成的种群，并在种群中的每个奖励下评估每一个策略，从而生成一个交叉适应度矩阵，该矩阵能够揭示自我掌握、迁移能力和功能多样性。种群级的规划器利用这些信息来选择父代奖励并发出有针对性的变异指令，而一个独立的变异器则将这些指令转化为经过验证的奖励程序。我们在一个离散的卡片沙盒和三个连续控制环境（Cart-Pole、Hopper等）中对Habitats进行了评估。
tldr: 提出了Habitats框架，通过维护奖励-策略对种群、构建交叉适应度矩阵并采用规划器与变异器分工协作的机制，实现了智能体可执行奖励目标的开放式演化，突破传统方法将目标设计与实现耦合所导致的行为局限。
en_tdlr: Habitats is a framework for open-ended evolution of executable agent objectives that maintains a population of reward-policy pairs and leverages a cross-fitness matrix with a Planner-Mutator division of labor to drive reward innovation beyond predefined tasks.
